articles.title: 5 Sci-Fi Series To Watch If You Love HBO's 'Lanterns'
articles.summary: HBO's Lanterns more than delivered when it comes to being both a great comic book series and a great piece of television. Not only did the series thrive thanks to the dynamic between Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), but it also managed to revitalize interest in the Green…
body: While Pierre is slated to return as John Stewart in 2027's Man of Tomorrow, there are still plenty of other series that manage to feature sci-fi tropes and elements alongside a compelling mystery or two. Here are five that make for the perfect binge-watch.

Much like Lanterns, Watchmen was met with mixed reception when it was first announced. Alan Moore's displeasure with adaptations of his work was well known at this point, and most fans asked why they should tune in when there was already a movie adaptation. However, Watchmen won over critics thanks to the way that it built on the original comic's events, while also weaving real history into its storytelling. It also weaves sci-fi elements into its narrative thanks to the presence of Doctor Manhattan, while still staying grounded. Fans looking for something that's similar to Lanterns definitely need to give Watchmen a look.
points: HBO's Lanterns more than delivered when it comes to being both a great comic book series and a great piece of television.

articles.title: 38 Years Later, Calvin and Hobbes' Lost Character Remains Bill Watterson's Biggest Failure
articles.summary: The author Lois McMaster Bujold has said that “the writer should always reserve the right to come up with a better idea.” That's a useful guideline for any reader to keep in mind.
body: Sometimes that decision is due to unexpected popularity, like how Opus and Bill the Cat quickly stole the spotlight in Bloom County. At other times, it might be due to shifting creative teams, real life concerns (i.e. Stephen King's near-death experience in 1999 became a major plot element of the last two books of his Dark Tower series), or that the author simply pivoted away from a plan that wasn't going to work out.

Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes has surprisingly few of those abandoned plot threads. It starts in close to the same place as it ends, as a joke-a-day strip with occasional deviations into high weirdness, art criticism, and accessible philosophy. There's a little more focus on Calvin's parents in the first couple of years of C&H and the art's a little looser, but the comic stays close to its original vision through its 10-year run.

The only real exception is in a two-week arc from 1988, where Calvin's uncle Max comes to visit his household. On a blind read through the comic, it's nothing that unusual, but the behind-the-scenes story of Uncle Max is a little more interesting.
points: The author Lois McMaster Bujold has said that “the writer should always reserve the right to come up with a better idea.
That's a useful guideline for any reader to keep in mind.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever World First Level 60 Character Hits Cap Three Days After Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is all about taking your time and exploring the world, rather than rushing to the endgame. But, despite the Forever team's insistence on taking your time and making friends, a WoW Forever player has already hit level 60.
body: Team JokerD, led by the eponymous streamer was the first team of characters to hit level 60, and the team was made up entirely of Undead characters and one Troll. The Undead race was important there, because Blizzard changed the Cannibalize ability to help you regenerate mana, which meant there was little to no downtime between massive pulls. I spent some time watching the streams of these speedrunners, and they'd gather entire groups of mobs to nuke them down with AoE abilities.

JokerD's claim to fame was being the world's first level 60 when World of Warcraft Classic launched back in 2019, so it's not super suprising that his team was the first to hit max level in Forever. There was plenty of competition this time around, but JokerD's team was pretty far ahead of the fray throughout the entire race. Even at the time of writing, the second place character who's not part of JokerD's team is Ksuper Worldfirst, who is still level 53.
points: World of Warcraft Forever is all about taking your time and exploring the world, rather than rushing to the endgame.
But, despite the Forever team's insistence on taking your time and making friends, a WoW Forever player has already hit level 60.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "Sniffing out the warehouses on Prawn Island"
articles.summary: Well, hello! I am once again wearing the Bertie hat in your usual host's absence, so joyous welcomes to our regular feature in which we talk about what we've been playing in recent times.
body: But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago. Bye!

Once again, I am finally playing a game from my backlog that I should've played years ago, and that's the delightful albeit dark card game Inscryption. There's so much more to this than you'd first expect, and I'm surprised the community has been able to keep the game's best bits under wraps for so long. Ultimately, nothing could've prepared me for Act 2, and my only real qualm with the whole experience is that I wish Act 2 had its own endless roguelike mode; you'd never be able to pull me away from it.

The game falters a little at the start of Act 3, I'll admit, and I've found myself very frustrated by what is an otherwise relatively easy time. This is down to me missing some rather useful earlier cards that I've since learnt would've made this final stretch much breezier, but oh well. I will still take down the Uberbots one way or another for the love of the game!

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Car Commercial Features New Look at Nightcrawler, Sparks Theories About Unannounced Heroes
articles.summary: An Avengers: Doomsday car commercial just revealed a first look at Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler in motion – and it may have teased a surprising cameo, too. Marvel Studios has played it safe when it comes to big reveals for next month's all-star superhero movie.
body: The car brand got in on the hype with a crossover commercial for Jeep 4x4s today. While similar videos are far from a new concept, it goes the extra mile by sending its cars through an onslaught of superhero antics themed around Avengers: Doomsday. It's not exactly footage from the movie, but between shots of Human Torch flyovers and shots of a war-torn X-Men school, Marvel did allow a first look at elements official trailers have hidden from viewers thus far.

Cumming's Kurt Wagner, a.k.a. Nightcrawler, is one character who was announced to be in the film ages ago, but we've seen so little of him so far. For some reason, this Jeep commercial marks our first official look at Nightcrawler using his teleportation powers in Avengers: Doomsday since 2003's X2. Although it's a quick moment that shows him leaping through cars, it's still nice to see him considered worth highlighting amongst such a jam-packed lineup of stars.

articles.title: The 8 Best Castlevania Games Of All Time, Ranked
articles.summary: Castlevania is one of the most beloved franchises in video game history, despite a period of 13 years when we didn’t see a new installment until the launch of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse earlier this year.
body: Over the years, the games have provided a variety of experiences, mixed with rich lore built on the vampire myth. With so many games available to choose from, it can be difficult to know where to begin if you haven’t touched the series in a while. Accordingly, here is our ranked list of the 8 best Castlevania games. It should make an excellent starting point.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Check our full Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse review for all the details, but the short version is this: you need to play the game. It respects the series’ history while mapping out a potential future we hope the developers will one day realize with follow-up titles. The 2.5D visuals give each area a new sense of depth, while enabling the satisfying Metroidvania mechanics players have enjoyed since Symphony of the Night changed the franchise forever. Fluid movement during combat, a killer soundtrack to match the moonlit ambience of the visuals, and a brave new hero all add up to one of the very finest entries the series has ever seen.

articles.title: 10 Essential GBA Games Still Disappointingly Missing From Nintendo Switch Online
articles.summary: When the original Game Boy came out, games like the ones people enjoyed on their NES were finally playable on the go, and players loved Nintendo for it. The green and black color palette was a bit of a bummer, but finally was rectified with the Game Boy Color.
body: Happily, many of the best games from the Game Boy Advance are available to enjoy today with a subscription to Switch Online with the Expansion Pack. However, there are still some absolute gems missing from that library. Here are 10 essential GBA games that belong on Switch Online.

Game Freak has worked on games besides Pokémon for years, and Drill Dozer is one of the developer’s early successes. Known as Screw Breaker in Japan, the platformer presented colorful stages that stood apart from other games in the genre and featured a young girl driving a powerful little tank. A rumble pack built into the cartridge let players feel as if they were dealing actual destruction in the stages they cleared. Unfortunately, the timing for Drill Dozer ’s launch wasn’t ideal. Nintendo was already in the middle of a big push to make its DS hardware a success, and didn’t do a lot of marketing for its final releases on older hardware.

articles.title: Can You Upgrade To GTA 6’s $100 Edition? Yes, And It’s Easy–Here’s How
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. If you're planning to buy the $80 edition but want to upgrade later to the $100 version, you might be interested to know if such a thing is possible. Thankfully, yes, it is-and it's very easy to do.
body: Rockstar will offer an "Ultimate Edition Upgrade" for $20, so for anyone who buys the $80 version and decides they do want the additional perks, they can upgrade. This applies to both the digital edition of GTA 6 that you can buy from the Xbox and PlayStation stores, as well the code-in-a-box physical edition.

The $100 Ultimate Edition, which is not sold in stores, includes a lot of extras, including vehicles, weapons, clothing for your in-game characters. The items are "threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia's story," Rockstar said, with new items becoming available "behind each chapter." Additionally, people who buy the $100 version get access to in-game businesses that won't be available to everyone else, including a hair salon, a tattoo parlor, a mod shop, and more.
Meanwhile, all preorders for GTA 6 come with the The Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+.

In other news, preloading for GTA 6 begins November 10, and that's good news considering the game weighs in at a whopping 212GB. The game officially unlocks at midnight local time, so pack your bags for New Zealand if you want to play it sooner.

articles.title: Donuts Beat AI: Nvidia Has Lost $1 Trillion+ In The Past Month, While Krispy Kreme Surges
articles.summary: Following the US midterm elections this week, shares of Nvidia--the world's No. 2 most valuable company by market cap behind Apple--slid downhill in a big way. In fact, more than $1 trillion has been wiped out from Nvidia's market cap since its peak in October.
body: Nvidia stock rebounded today, November 6, following the huge selloff on November 5 that also affected numerous other AI and technology stocks. However, Nvidia is still lagging behind Krispy Kreme in terms of growth in 2026.

That's right, shares of Krispy Kreme stock--$DNUT--are up about 3% in 2026, compared to negative returns for Nvidia this year. If you invested $1,000 into both $DNUT and $NVDA this year, you'd be making money on donuts and losing money on AI.

Krispy Kreme's stock price exploded on November 5 after a solid earnings report, but has moderated since. In any event, Krispy Kreme is beating Nvidia so far in 2026 based on the percent gain for its stock price.

To be sure, Nvidia and Krispy Kreme are not competitors in the market and their stock prices are not comparable except for the purpose of some laughs. Nvidia, with a market cap of more than $4.5 trillion, remains a juggernaut that captures the world's attention. Krispy Kreme, meanwhile, has a market cap of under $1 billion, but they do make a damn good glazed donut. Krispy Kreme also rolled out a new line of Pokemon donuts this year, and they're delicious.

articles.title: You Can Finally Drive A Dreamcast, Thanks To Sonic
articles.summary: Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is gearing up for a second year of action, and while you can expect new courses, modes, and characters to join the game, the real headline act here is the new cars coming to it.
body: The new cars are based on the Sega Genesis (or Mega Drive for anyone who lived outside the US), the Sega Saturn, and Sega's final home console, the Dreamcast. According to the Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds development team, the idea was to incorporate design elements that would instantly remind players of each console into their respective vehicle frames, like the rounded form of the Dreamcast or the angular silhouettes and subdued tones of the Saturn. The team even went so far as to recreate the Dreamcast’s Visual Memory Unit using original reference data from that era.

"Rather than directly recreating the hardware itself, we translated rounded forms into fenders and nose sections, while angular lines became body panels and hoods, adding the sense of speed expected from a racing machine," the development team explained in a PlayStation Blog post. "While preserving recognizable colors and components from each system, we also designed around the game’s front-and-rear combination mechanic, incorporating the fun of pairing consoles and controllers into the vehicles themselves."

articles.title: Mass Effect Is Getting A New Art Collection At A Difficult Time For Its Fans
articles.summary: This year's annual Mass Effect Day looks to be somber in light of the studio behind the games, BioWare, being shut down last month. But while no new Mass Effect games are currently on the horizon, you can celebrate its legacy through some classy art prints that are going up for sale ahead of N7…
body: Moor-Art says it began collaborating with BioWare over a year ago to release a new selection of limited-edition posters. "What began as a celebration of an ongoing saga now feels like the bastion in the continuation of a studio's legacy," the studio said in a press release.

The collection from Moor-Art is inspired by the characters and worlds of Mass Effect, with the original artwork being produced by acclaimed artists and Mass Effect die-hard fans Matt Essom and Dan Mumford. The designs will also be available as T-shirts. The first one is by Essom, and Moor-Art says this illustration captures the spirit and emotional depth of the series, as well as the bonds forged on the Normandy as her crew traveled to unknown worlds. This will be limited to 200 hand-numbered prints worldwide, plus 30 Giclée prints with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist.

articles.title: Updated Xbox PC app promises 60% faster loading and easier access to games, but CEO Asha Sharma says there's "plenty more to do"
articles.summary: The Xbox PC app hasn't had the best track record in recent years, but Microsoft is promising that it's now much faster and easier to use than before.
body: Starting today, anyone part of the Xbox Insiders program can try out the new improvements. According to Microsoft, the updated Xbox PC app now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50% faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65% faster. The company acknowledged that performance can vary based on your set up, internet connection, device, and so on.

The rest of the update involves "simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organise your games," according to Xbox Wire, while social features are now included in the main navigation menu so you can start playing or chatting with friends quicker.

A faster Xbox PC app is certainly nice for players who regularly use it, though it's still missing a lot of the features that make Steam the go-to place to buy PC games. CEO Asha Sharma called the update "a meaningful improvement," but acknowledged there's still "plenty more to do."
Microsoft also said "it's easier to find what you're looking for" using the app's search function, and refreshed game cards and animations should give the platform "a cleaner look and feel."
points: The Xbox PC app hasn't had the best track record in recent years, but Microsoft is promising that it's now much faster and easier to use than before.

videos.title: Want a New Elder Scrolls? Play Queen's Domain, the Old-School RPG Inspired by King's Field
videos.summary: Queen's Domain impressions by Michael Higham, played on PC (also available on PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2)
body: "I'm a sucker for a good throwback to the early polygonal 32-bit era – Mouthwashing, Signalis, Crow Country, and Boltgun 2 are some recent favorites that come to mind. The latest one I've locked in on is Queen's Domain, a fantasy RPG that's as if an Elder Scrolls game was made for the PlayStation 1. Actually, it's explicitly inspired by FromSoftware's pre-Dark Souls series King's Field, where slow, deliberate first-person combat and exploration complemented punishing difficulty (which would later become FromSoft's signature, of course). But as much as Queen's Domain draws clear inspiration or shares similarities, it's a singular experience in 2026 that, from what I've played so far, wields the intended friction of an old-school game wonderfully."

videos.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 - PS5/Pro/Xbox Series X|S Tech Review - PSSR Has Pros and Cons
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: The first of the series to purely target PS5 and Xbox Series consoles, Modern Warfare 4 makes the most of the generational leap with benefits to its COD Engine tech. Today the focus is on the PS5 Pro upgrades - specifically giving us improved effects, reflections and shading - with ruminations on its PSSR upscaler. Later, Xbox Series S gets its time in the spotlight, with testing across both its 120Hz and 60Hz modes.

body: Suzy Day is a talented singer who dreams of making it big. This is a song she creates together with Daito in postwar Atami, during a time when foreign cultures and people from overseas were beginning to flow into Japan and a new culture was taking shape.
